homeTitle: Voters have the right to know the plan in advance
problem: Parties ask citizens to entrust them with a vote, yet often leave the most consequential agreements until after the election.
solution: Contract in Advance proposes one transparency standard. Every party receives the same questions about possible coalitions, the size of government, compliance with court rulings, the inquiry into 7 October, and the first steps after the election.

privacyBody:
We collect only the information needed to verify support, generate aggregate metrics, and moderate replies. Personalized appeal text is never stored.

We do not publish personal information without consent, sell data, or send appeals for you. Administrators may access submitted data only for campaign operation and moderation.

You may request deletion below. Operational backups are retained under the documented schedule. Contact the campaign operator for privacy questions.

slogan: The rules must be known before the vote.
subtitle: Before the election, parties should disclose the coalitions they would join, the shape of the government they would form, their commitments to the law, and their programme for the first 100 days.
neutrality: The platform does not recommend how to vote. It lets a citizen support the transparency requirements and send a specific question to a party of their own choosing.

aboutBody:
Contract in Advance is an independent civic platform concerned with the transparency of party commitments before an election.

The project is not a political party, does not field candidates, and does not recommend voting for or against any list. It puts the same core set of questions to every party, lets users compose and send their own messages, does not hand any supporter database to parties, and does not store the link between a verified supporter and the recipient they chose.

### Funding

As at the date of publication the project is funded by: [personal funds / funds of a registered organisation / other]. The funding source, project costs, services provided free of charge and potential conflicts of interest are published. Until separate legal and accounting arrangements are in place, the project does not accept donations for electoral activity.

### Connections

Directors and editors disclose paid work for parties, official party positions, significant services to candidates, and participation in campaign headquarters.
methodologyBody:
Every figure is counted and published separately.

### Verified support

A record counts as verified once the user has confirmed the email address. To prevent double counting, an irreversible or pseudonymised identifier of the address may be retained.

### Generated appeal

An appeal counts as generated when the user has chosen a recipient and questions and received prepared text. This does not mean it was sent.

### Opening an app

Counted separately: opening email; opening WhatsApp; copying text. None of these confirms delivery.

### Reported sending

This figure reflects a user's statement that they completed the sending. It is not called a "delivered appeal".

### Submitted reply

Material counts as submitted once the user has uploaded it. This does not mean the reply is official or accurate.

### Prohibited analytics

The platform does not publish or use a party's number of "potential voters", a user's past voting history, presumed future vote, political profile, or audiences segmented by political view.
